description: High performance, shrinkage compensated, high-flow micro-concrete and thick section grout
whereToUse: For pile top treatment and re-profiling, column jacketing, concrete structural repairs, and where particular thickness and void configuration requires the use of a high-flow micro-concrete or grout, for gaps up to 220 mm.
Structural reinstatement of new and old reinforced concrete elements such as beams and columns
Particularly suitable for reinstatement of honeycombed concrete and or areas of congested reinforcement
Reinstatement of floor beams and slabs
Grouting of machine and turbine baseplates, bridge bearings, and crane rails
notFor: Do not use Mapegrout ME05 on smooth concrete surfaces; roughen such surfaces
Do not use Mapegrout ME05 for precision anchoring (use Mapefill GP ME or Mapefill SP ME)
Do not use Mapegrout ME05 for applications on vertical surfaces without formwork (use Mapegrout T60 ME or Mapegrout T80)
Do not add cement or any other additives to Mapegrout ME05
Do not add more water than the recommended dosage

notes: 1) No kg/m2 per mm or per cm figure is printed anywhere; the only consumption figure is '12.7 liters per 25 kg.' Any kg/m2 figure would have to be derived (e.g. from the printed mix density 2200 kg/m³) and is not in the sheet. 2) The water sentence is printed 'Pour 3.1-3.3 Iitres' with a capital letter I in place of the first l of 'litres' (a typo in the source); the consumption value is copied that way so that it matches the text - display it as 'litres'. The sentence does not say per bag. 3) Three water figures: 12.4-13.2 kg per 100 kg (application table), 3.1-3.3 litres (prose) and 13% (laboratory mix in the technical data table). They agree with one another if the prose figure is per 25 kg bag. 4) Product name is printed both 'Mapegrout ME05' and 'Mapegrout ME 05'. 5) Thickness: 'for gaps up to 220 mm', 'recommended for voids up to 220 mm' and table 'Application thickness: 15 - 220 mm' (printed with a long dash); greater thicknesses 'may be achieved' subject to MAPEI advice. 6) In technicalData the strength rows combine the three ages into one row (1, 7 and 28 days in that order); the EN 1504-3 R4 requirement printed beside them is '> 45 MPa' at 28 days. 7) The 'Composition of the mix' string comes from the layout file (label and values are separated in the reading-order file). 8) No consumption formula and no consumption table are printed.
